name: Rituximab (Rituxan/MabThera)
reasoning: Querying ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed for pivotal trials, endpoints, and attrition signals…
Cross-checking openFDA + FDA approval records for the exact regulatory pathway…
Connecting research → clinical → regulatory; every claim 3-vote cross-checked, unsourced items flagged.

claims.text: Modality rationale / mechanism of action: binding of rituximab to CD20 triggers three distinct cell-destruction mechanisms — direct apoptotic signaling, complement activation, and cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC).
claims.quote: Mechanisms of cell destruction that have been demonstrated to be activated by rituximab binding to CD20 include direct signaling of apoptosis, complement activation and cell-mediated cytotoxicity.

claims.text: Independent U.S. government (NCI) corroboration that rituximab (Rituxan) is a CD20-directed antibody that eliminates malignant B cells, confirming target and mechanism.
claims.quote: rituximab (Rituxan) to specifically bind to CD20 and eliminate cancerous B cells.

claims.text: Competitive set: the glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 successor obinutuzumab challenged rituximab head-to-head in first-line follicular lymphoma (GALLIUM) and significantly improved progression-free survival over rituximab-based chemoimmunotherapy — evidence the anti-CD20 class has advanced beyond the incumbent.
claims.quote: hazard ratio for progression, relapse, or death, 0.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.51 to 0.85; P=0.001

claims.text: Pivotal single-agent trial in relapsed low-grade/follicular B-cell NHL (McLaughlin et al., J Clin Oncol 1998): 166 patients across 31 centers received IDEC-C2B8 (rituximab) 375 mg/m2 weekly x4; the intent-to-treat overall response rate was 48%, with projected median time to progression of 13.0 months. This was the registrational efficacy basis for the 1997 indication.

Pivotal randomized trial in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (GELA LNH-98.5): the first randomized study comparing R-CHOP vs CHOP in 399 patients aged 60-80; adding rituximab improved 10-year overall survival to 43.5% vs 27.6% (and 10-year PFS 36.5% vs 20%), the practice-changing survival result that expanded rituximab into aggressive lymphoma.
claims.quote: the 10-year overall survival was 43.5% compared with 27.6%

claims.text: Attrition signal (failed primary endpoint): in the randomized RESORT/ECOG E4402 trial in low-tumor-burden follicular lymphoma, a maintenance-rituximab dosing strategy did NOT beat simple re-treatment on the primary endpoint of time to treatment failure (median TTF 4.3 yr maintenance vs 3.9 yr re-treatment; P=.54), showing that more intensive rituximab dosing failed to demonstrate superiority.
claims.quote: the estimated median TTF was 3.9 years for patients receiving RR and 4.3 years for those receiving MR (P = .54).

claims.text: Exact FDA approval: rituximab was approved by the U.S. FDA on November 26, 1997 — the first monoclonal antibody approved for the treatment of lymphoma. (No expedited-program label such as Accelerated Approval, Breakthrough Therapy, Priority Review, Fast Track, RTOR, or Project Orbis is asserted; the approval predates RTOR/2018 and Project Orbis/2019, and none was verifiable from primary sources.)
claims.quote: approved by the US Food and Drug Administration on November 26, 1997

claims.text: Exact original approved indication wording: relapsed or refractory, CD20-positive, B-cell, low-grade or follicular non-Hodgkin's lymphoma — precise verbatim label language, tying the regulatory grant directly to the CD20 target and the McLaughlin pivotal population.
claims.quote: relapsed or refractory, CD20-positive, B-cell, low-grade or follicular non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (LG/F NHL)
